2609.10049.title: MedDeID enables locally governed clinical-text de-identification from real or synthetic training data
2609.10049.paper_summary: Clinical notes contain personally identifiable information (PII), restricting reuse for research and medical AI, especially when data cannot leave an institution. We developed MedDeID, an on-premises framework combining in-house annotation and synthetic-note generation with model training, inference, pseudonymisation and evaluation. On an independently annotated, adjudicated 300-note Dutch hospital benchmark, a hospital-trained compact transformer detected 98.9% of identifying text while redacting 0.24% of text outside annotated identifiers; a synthetic-only counterpart detected 96.1%. On 100 primary-care notes, the synthetic-trained model achieved higher recall than the hospital-trained model (90.3% versus 87.0%) and greater robustness to identifier-format perturbations. An English instantiation trained without real text detected 99.7% and 98.9% of annotated identifier characters on two external synthetic benchmarks. These results demonstrate transfer of the workflow to another language, but not clinical English performance. MedDeID provides a route to locally governed de-identification using real or synthetic training data.
2609.10049.paper_summary_zh: 臨床筆記包含個人可識別信息（PII），限制了其在研究和醫療 AI 中的重用，特別是當數據無法離開機構時。我們開發了 MedDeID，一個本地框架，結合了內部註釋和合成筆記生成，並進行模型訓練、推斷、假名化和評估。在一個獨立註釋、裁定的 300 篇荷蘭醫院基準中，一個經醫院訓練的緊湊型Transformer檢測到了 98.9% 的識別文本，同時對註釋標識符以外的文本進行了 0.24% 的編輯；而一個僅使用合成數據的對應模型檢測到了 96.1%。在 100 篇初級護理筆記中，合成訓練模型的召回率高於醫院訓練模型（90.3% 對 87.0%），並對標識符格式擾動具有更大的穩健性。一個未使用真實文本訓練的英語實例在兩個外部合成基準上檢測到了 99.7% 和 98.9% 的註釋標識符字符。這些結果顯示了工作流程向另一種語言的轉移，但不包括臨床英語的表現。MedDeID 提供了一條使用真實或合成訓練數據進行本地治理去識別化的途徑。
